intent.oneSentence: A branched electrical strike reaches a point, where a rooted fire prepares, rises and burns out.
intent.firstRead: A brief electrical event followed by a longer rooted fire.
intent.mustNotReadAs: A continuous lightning hose, a recolored water flow or an immediate universal explosion.
intent.useContext: A native-size opt-in authoring example on a dark background; tests demonstrate source connectivity, not automatic art quality.

readability.primaryShape: One branched electrical channel followed by a rooted rising flame.
readability.depthAndOverlap: Use existing back/front material passes; the action and response overlap only during their authored causal transition.
readability.contrast: Material colors remain distinct; no added exposure or glow budget.
readability.secondaryDetailBudget: Original generator counts and lifetimes are unchanged; the fire example hides its spark layer so its volumes remain the secondary response.

mechanics.driver: The lightning arrival is 0.23 s, so fire preparation starts at 0.23 s. Fire release follows its own 0.28 s preparation, at 0.51 s. The fire source (0,12) is translated by y=-12 to the strike point (0,0). Sparks are hidden in the fire cue so lightning branches and fire volumes retain separate roles; this is an existing diagnostic layer option, not a new particle budget.
mechanics.direction: Lightning descends to (0,0); fire begins its preparation there after arrival, rises against gravity and leaves cooling matter.
mechanics.weightAndMaterial: Retain the existing generator behavior for each material. No new fluid, heat-transfer or collision simulation is introduced.
mechanics.causalChain: A branched electrical strike reaches a point, where a rooted fire prepares, rises and burns out.
mechanics.endingRule: Both sources run to their natural endings; the sequence is empty at 3.16 seconds.
mechanics.exaggerationAndLimits: This is an authored multi-material composition and a reusable data connection, not automatic choreography, artistic certification or Niagara simulation.

phases.name: preparation
phases.action: The discharge is not yet released.
phases.cause: An electrical source precedes the return current.

phases.name: action
phases.action: A branched leader establishes a path to the contact point.
phases.cause: The generator follows its existing strike timing.

phases.name: response
phases.action: Fire preparation starts at arrival; rising emission begins at 0.51 s and ends at 1.81 s.
phases.cause: Authored delayed material response at the same source point.
phases.visibleCue: Electrical repeat fades while rooted flame becomes dominant.

phases.name: ending
phases.action: The fire stops feeding, remaining volumes cool and the final frame is empty.
phases.cause: Both independent finite effects have ended.
phases.visibleCue: No light-only residue at the endpoint.

references.observed: The JSON stores material intent, source placement, timing and layer selection.
references.application: Use existing generated renderers through the existing Sequence scheduler.
references.limits: Intended meaning only; native still review and full-speed playback observations must be recorded separately.
